## Introduction 

In this notebook, we are reverse engineering the story, [CEOs gave heavily during legislative session, exposing loophole in NC's fundraising ban](https://www.wral.com/archive/17716104/)

## Load libraries

Loading required libraries for this analysis.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Turn off scientific notation
options(scipen=999)

# load your libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(refinr)
library(janitor)
library(stringr)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)

```

## Load and Cleaning Data

In this section, describe the source of the data, write a basic data dictionary for data you are working with, and discuss any caveats or issues you discovered working with this data. 

```{r}
# Load required data

nc_finance_data <- read_excel("data/donors0103-0701.xlsx")

# Path to data should be loaded from folder "data" i.e. read_csv("data/name_of_data.csv")

# Clean required data and prepare for analysis if needed. 

nc_finance_data <- nc_finance_data |> 
  rename(name_clean = "name-clean")

```

## Sentences to Engineer
In this notebook, we are reverse engineering five sentences from the story.

### Sentence 1

* **Sentence text**: The co-chief executives at a Georgia firm that brokers tax credits put $41,000 into the campaign accounts of North Carolina General Assembly members during the last regular legislative session. 
* **Analysis summary**: We filtered by names of the two CEOs, GEORGE LEWIS STROBEL II and ROBIN E DELMER for the dates of the short legislative session in 2018, which was from May 16 to June 29. We also filtered for donations made to candidates. We found that, combined, the two men had donated a combined $41,250, which matches the original finding exactly.

```{r}
# Put code to reverse engineer sentence here
nc_finance_data_session <- nc_finance_data |> 
  filter(between(date, as.Date("2018-05-16"), as.Date("2018-06-29")))

nc_finance_data_session |> 
  filter((name_clean == "GEORGE LEWIS STROBEL II" | name_clean == "ROBIN E DELMER") & source == "candidates") |> 
  group_by(name_clean) |> 
  summarise(
    total = sum(amount)
  )


# Display results of code below this codeblock

```
